title: Towards Understanding and Mitigating Social Biases in Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures stereotypical and harmful representational biases against religious groups in language model text generation. This includes automatically detecting bias-sensitive tokens (e.g., 'terrorists' for Islam) and evaluating the 'regard' of generated sentences for different religious prompts.
findings: The study found that GPT-2 perpetuates harmful stereotypes, particularly against Muslims. For instance, automatically detected bias-sensitive tokens for Islam included 'terrorists', 'jihad', and 'terror', with human annotators judging 32% of the top-ranked words as showing severely negative bias. The proposed debiasing method, A-INLP, was shown to be effective in mitigating these religious biases in generated text while largely preserving text quality, as demonstrated by automated metrics and human evaluations.
references: Ricardo Baeza-Yates. Data and algorithmic bias in the web. In Proceedings of the 8th ACM Conference on Web Science, pages 1–1, 2016.
